campaign.title: Near-square complementary-divisor gate for the lower M1 discrepancy

resource_policy.literature_policy: Use no new theorem unless a primary source matches the prescribed centre, sharp sqrt(X) divisor truncation, chi_4 coefficient, one-sided Fourier wavelet, pointwise real-X norm, and required power. Do not import the desired circle estimate through a short-interval bound.

frozen_target.question: After a target-safe localization of the exact Round-121 discrepancy wavelet, does the near-square complementary-divisor involution give a noninvertible signed gain, a strict target-safe branch, or a rigorous self-return?
frozen_target.reference_formula: B_flat^(N)=sum_(k in Z)D_N(k)W_(R,y)(k), where D_N(k)=sum_(d<=y)chi_4(d)(floor((N+k)/d)-floor(N/d)-k/d), W_(R,y)(k)=hat J(k)-hat J(k+1), J(t)=eta(yt)V_low(4R^2t^2)/t, and the target is B_flat^(N)<<R X^epsilon.
quantities: X large real, R=X^(1/4), y=floor(sqrt X), N=floor X
all k in Z before a proved target-safe tail deletion
K_(R,y)(t)=J_(R,y)(t)(1-e(-t)) and its uniform Fourier envelope
m=N+k positive on the localized window
m=2^a m_0 with m_0 odd and every a>=0
fixed cutoff d<=y versus complementary threshold m_0/y
m_0 mod 4 character sign, square ties, central divisor band, and hard d=y sample
signed k-wavelet retained across every parity and complement branch
full r_2/4 coefficient plus exact complementary tail, never one without the other
all Round-121 normalization, real-X amplitudes, and downstream owner restrictions

completion_criteria: Prove a uniform Fourier envelope and target-safe far-k tail for W_(R,y).
Keep m=N+k positive and quantify the exact surviving k-window.
Derive the complementary-divisor identity for every 2-adic valuation and odd residue class.
Price all strict/weak cutoff boundaries, square ties, and the central divisor band.
Keep the complete signed k-sum until a quantitative inequality is obtained.
Audit whether the full r_2 coefficient invokes the circle problem or only a proved input.
Distinguish a noninvertible gain from reconstruction of the Round-121 cone or Round-65 crossing return.
Prove the complete target, a strict target-safe subpackage, a signed power saving/inverse theorem, or a rigorous self-return/no-go with the smallest survivor.
State exactly what follows for lower GAR, GAR, blockwise M1, M9-M2, endpoint uniformity, M9, and every exponent.

tasks.target: Independently localize the exact discrepancy wavelet, derive every complementary-divisor branch, and prove a target, strict subpackage, inverse theorem, or smallest rigorous self-return without nonblind history.
excluded_context: all Round-64 through Round-122 nonblind artifacts
required_output: A uniform wavelet-tail derivation and complete 2-adic divisor involution.
A complete estimate, strict target-safe package, inverse theorem, or exact self-return/no-go.
A promote, retain, revise, reject, or no-change recommendation.

tasks.target: Derive the literal Fourier localization and all 2-adic complementary-divisor branches, then seek a noninvertible signed inequality on the complete near-square wavelet.
required_output: Exact Fourier-envelope and 2-adic complement formulas with capacity table.
A target estimate, strict signed gain, inverse theorem, or smallest exact return.

tasks.target: Hostilely audit wavelet-tail uniformity, every parity and central boundary, circular use of the circle estimate, self-return to prior cones, false unsigned analogues, and all claimed downstream implications.
required_output: A pass/fail seam table and capacity/circularity controls.
The maximal safe theorem or fatal correction and smallest survivor.

review_seams.requirement: The difference weight is derived from the explicit one-sided sample interpolant, with uniform norms and a target-safe discarded tail.
Every retained m=N+k is positive and near-square at the quantified scale; d|0 and negative-index conventions are not silently dropped.
The divisor complement is exact for every 2-adic valuation, odd character residue, strict cutoff, square tie, and central divisor.
The full divisor coefficient and complementary tail are inserted together exactly once.
The k-wavelet and all parity branches remain jointly signed until a quantified inequality is proved.
No bound assumes the quarter circle discrepancy, an equivalent short-interval theorem, or a stronger unproved full-divisor estimate.
Complementary inversion, r_2 completion, or Fourier reconstruction is not called a gain if it returns to the accepted cone or unmatched-crossing functional.
A lower-GAR reduction or subpackage is not promoted to GAR, blockwise M1, M9-M2, endpoint uniformity, M9, or an exponent without its exact graph bridge.
